scope: Four anonymous GET requests, three complete documentation lists. Full bodies preserved for exact original-entry matching; no credentials or write requests.

data.title: Two-component architecture: one shared reporter, ten interchangeable sensing modules
data.value:
Insect odorant receptors are **not GPCRs**. A tuning receptor and the obligate co-receptor Orco
assemble into a heteromeric **ligand-gated cation channel**; odorant binding opens the pore
directly, with no second messenger in between. Orco also chaperones the tuning receptor to the
plasma membrane — without it the tuning receptor stays in the ER.

Two consequences shape this collection:

1. **The read-out can be shared.** Every tuning receptor needs the same Orco, and the channel
   conducts Ca²⁺, so one calcium-indicator–Orco fusion serves as the read-out for all of them. That
   is `BBa_26E11Z80`, the only part in the collection carrying a reporter.
2. **Specificity is the only interchangeable layer.** The ten sensing modules differ from each other
   in nothing but the tuning receptor CDS. Swapping one for another changes what the cell detects
   and leaves the read-out, the optics, the calculation and the controls untouched.

A working sensor is always **two co-transfected parts**: one sensing module plus `BBa_26E11Z80`.
Neither is a device alone.

### Collection-wide design decisions

| Decision | Applies to | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| **Codon-optimised for human expression** | all 11 receptor CDSs, incl. Orco | Zboray *et al.* (2023) used **wild-type** OR sequences and identified translation as a likely bottleneck, writing that "functional OR protein expression can be improved by codon optimization of OR genes instead of using wild type sequences". This collection takes that route; it is the largest deliberate difference from that study. |
| **EMCV IRES + mCherry** on every sensing module | the 10 modules | One transcript, two separate proteins. mCherry is translated cap-independently, so red fluorescence reports that the transcript reached the cytoplasm **even when the receptor is non-functional** — the case that is otherwise undiagnosable. A 2A peptide was rejected because it leaves a residual peptide on the receptor. |
| **GCCACC Kozak** on every ORF | all composites | strong mammalian initiation |
| **No promoter, no polyA** | all parts | portable coding parts; the host vector sets expression level and induction. Every part here needs a promoter and terminator from its host vector. |
| **Receptors supplied both as bare CDS and as a module** | 10 + 10 parts | the bare CDS (e.g. `BBa_26VGDFA1`) for teams assembling into their own context; the module (e.g. `BBa_26ZAGFK0`) as a ready bicistronic unit |

The geometry of the reporter fusion — why the indicator is at the **N**-terminus, why the linker is
the length it is — is intrinsic to `BBa_26E11Z80` and documented there. The inverted membrane
topology that forces it is documented on `BBa_26LWIKBQ` (DmOrco CDS).

### Where the sequences come from

Nothing here was cloned from an organism, evolved, or computationally designed. The eleven receptor
coding sequences are the **native *Drosophila melanogaster* protein sequences back-translated with
human codon usage** and synthesised; each encodes a protein identical to its FlyBase reference.

| part | receptor | FlyBase gene | transcript | RefSeq protein | aa |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BBa_26LWIKBQ` | Orco | FBgn0037324 | FBtr0078794 | NP_524235 | 486 |
| `BBa_26VGDFA1` | Or7a | FBgn0030016 | FBtr0071186 | NP_511081 | 413 |
| `BBa_26HTXB02` | Or19a | FBgn0041626 | FBtr0070029 | NP_525013 | 387 |
| `BBa_26AIIWHV` | Or22a | FBgn0026398 | FBtr0077873 | NP_523453 | 397 |
| `BBa_26HJ1RUT` | Or35a | FBgn0028946 | FBtr0080781 | NP_723916 | 409 |
| `BBa_26UHN7NT` | Or42a | FBgn0033041 | FBtr0086052 | NP_523622 | 406 |
| `BBa_26OJ8HGO` | Or59b | FBgn0034865 | FBtr0072021 | NP_523822 | 398 |
| `BBa_26XXP4K7` | Or67a | FBgn0036009 | FBtr0076375 | NP_524005 | 407 |
| `BBa_26ACVV3R` | Or67b | FBgn0036019 | FBtr0076420 | NP_524007 | 421 |
| `BBa_26DVVZIA` | Or85b | FBgn0037590 | FBtr0081900 | NP_524279 | 390 |
| `BBa_26DG1NPK` | Or98a | FBgn0039551 | FBtr0085226 | NP_524536 | 397 |

The non-receptor components:

| part | origin |
|---|---|
| `BBa_26QHYP02` GCaMP6f | derived from Addgene **#40755**; indicator described by Chen *et al.* (2013) |
| `BBa_26E21OEQ` (GGGGS)₃ linker | fully synthetic; the three repeats use **diversified synonymous codons** so the DNA carries no tandem repeat, which is a common cause of synthesis failure and polymerase slippage |
| `BBa_262WP16P` RSET leader | the N-terminal leader of the **pRSET** vector series (Invitrogen) |
| EMCV IRES (inside the 10 modules) | encephalomyocarditis virus internal ribosome entry site, wild-type |
| mCherry (inside the 10 modules) | Shaner *et al.* (2004) |

All constructs were **synthesised by GenScript** and delivered in an IP-free version of the
pcDNA3.1(+) backbone.

### The odorant panel that was actually tested, and what was known about it

Six compounds plus the Orco agonist were tested. Two of the six were lost to the gain
fault (collection *Experiment* entry). This is what the literature says about each of them **for the
receptors in this collection** — responses reported for receptors not in this collection are not
relevant and are excluded:

| compound | class | published response on a receptor in **this** collection |
|---|---|---|
| **VUAA1**, 50 µM | synthetic Orco agonist | activates every Orco-containing line; the positive control for the whole platform (Jones *et al.* 2011) |
| **isopentyl acetate** *(lost to gain fault)* | ester | **Or98a, 0.31** VUAA1-normalised at 100 µM — the strongest published match in the panel |
| **2-heptanone** | methyl ketone | **Or85b, 0.55** at 100 µM — Or85b's reference ligand, EC₅₀ **68.9 µM**; also Or98a 0.11 |
| **3-octanol** | secondary alcohol | Or98a, 0.13 at 100 µM |
| **benzaldehyde** | aromatic aldehyde | **none.** Reported for Or49b (0.23) and Or10a (0.17), neither of which is in this collection |
| **ethyl propionate** *(lost to gain fault)* | ester | **none reported** |
| **valeric acid** | carboxylic acid | **none reported.** No carboxylic acid appears anywhere in the responsive ligand set of Zboray *et al.* (2023), for any of their seven lines |

Three consequences follow, and all three are uncomfortable:

1. **Only two of the eleven receptors in this collection had any published reason to respond to this
   panel** — Or85b and Or98a. For the other nine the panel was a blind screen.
2. **The one compound with the strongest published match, isopentyl acetate on Or98a, is one of the
   two that the gain fault destroyed.** The loss was not two arbitrary compounds; it was the
   best-predicted odorant × receptor combination on the plate.
3. **The panel was dosed by a dilution factor inherited from fly work, and the resulting molar
   concentrations are unknown.** The supplied stock's concentration was never recorded, so none of
   these published EC₅₀ values can be compared against what was actually delivered. See the
   *Experiment* entry.

The reasoning that led to this particular set of six is not recorded in this documentation; a future
team should choose by EC₅₀ and by the receptors actually in hand.

### Parts in this collection

**Read-out (1)** — `BBa_26E11Z80` GCaMP6f-(GGGGS)₃-DmOrco, 2,862 bp

**Sensing modules (10)**, all `<OR>-IRES-mCherry` —
`BBa_26ZAGFK0` Or7a · `BBa_2629NIWH` Or19a · `BBa_26WOX4B1` Or22a · `BBa_26LLF3LM` Or35a ·
`BBa_26Q1Q094` Or42a · `BBa_26Y7CI2H` Or59b · `BBa_265G8CE1` Or67a · `BBa_269VSDDR` Or67b ·
`BBa_26K1TU11` Or85b · `BBa_26TZLBMJ` Or98a

**Tuning receptor CDSs (10)** —
`BBa_26VGDFA1` Or7a · `BBa_26HTXB02` Or19a · `BBa_26AIIWHV` Or22a · `BBa_26HJ1RUT` Or35a ·
`BBa_26UHN7NT` Or42a · `BBa_26OJ8HGO` Or59b · `BBa_26XXP4K7` Or67a · `BBa_26ACVV3R` Or67b ·
`BBa_26DVVZIA` Or85b · `BBa_26DG1NPK` Or98a

**Components of the read-out fusion (4)** —
`BBa_26LWIKBQ` DmOrco CDS · `BBa_26QHYP02` GCaMP6f · `BBa_26E21OEQ` (GGGGS)₃ linker ·
`BBa_262WP16P` RSET leader

### References

1. Zboray K, Mohamed Mahmoud M, Pató A, *et al.* Stable cell lines expressing *Drosophila* odorant receptors for the detection of plant pathogen-related volatile organic compounds. *Sci Rep* **13**, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4
2. Jones PL, Pask GM, Rinker DC, Zwiebel LJ. Functional agonism of insect odorant receptor ion channels. *PNAS* **108**, 8821–8825 (2011).
3. Chen T-W, Wardill TJ, Sun Y, *et al.* Ultrasensitive fluorescent proteins for imaging neuronal activity. *Nature* **499**, 295–300 (2013).
4. Shaner NC, Campbell RE, Steinbach PA, *et al.* Improved monomeric red, orange and yellow fluorescent proteins derived from *Discosoma* sp. red fluorescent protein. *Nat Biotechnol* **22**, 1567–1572 (2004).
5. FlyBase — https://flybase.org/ (accessions in the table above)
6. DoOR 2.0 — Database of Odorant Responses. http://neuro.uni-konstanz.de/DoOR/

data.title: Plate-reader calcium assay: conditions, two-round addition, calculation, gain QC
data.value:
Every number in this collection comes from **one experiment, run on 2026-10-10**: a single 96-well
plate, one well per condition.

### Chassis and transfection

| | |
|---|---|
| Cells | HEK293, uncoated 96-well black-wall clear-bottom plate (GREINER 96 F-BOTTOM) |
| Transfection | **transient co-transfection** of one sensing module + `BBa_26E11Z80` |
| On-plate controls | column 11 = `BBa_26E11Z80` alone (no tuning receptor); column 12 = **untransfected** HEK293 |

### Reader

| | |
|---|---|
| Instrument | BMG LABTECH **CLARIOstar Plus**, SMART Control / MARS |
| Mode | fluorescence intensity, plate mode, kinetic, **bottom optic** |
| Optics | Ex **482-16** / Dichroic **LP 504** / Em **530-40** |
| Focal height | **−4.1 mm** |
| Flashes per well per cycle | 20 |
| Settling time | 0.5 s |
| Cycle time | **12 s** (instrument minimum for this layout: 10 s) |
| Enhanced dynamic range | **off**; full scale 260,000 RFU |
| Temperature control | **off** (ambient) |
| Shaking | none |

### Assay buffer

140 mM NaCl · 5 mM KCl · **2 mM CaCl₂** · 1 mM MgCl₂ · 5 mM HEPES-Na · 20 mM glucose, pH 7.3.
Recipe after Zboray *et al.* (2023). The Ca²⁺ is load-bearing: that study abolished the Orco-agonist response in
Ca²⁺-free buffer and in Ca²⁺-free buffer with EGTA, which is what establishes that the fluorescence
rise reports **extracellular** Ca²⁺ entering through the channel.

### The two-round addition — and why it matters more than it looks

| step | action | read | cycles | volume in well |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | plate the cells in assay buffer | **F0a** — baseline | 5 | 100 µL |
| 2 | **+ 50 µL plain assay buffer** — *round 1, the vehicle control* | **blank** | 15 | 150 µL |
| 3 | — | **F0b** — new baseline | 5 | 150 µL |
| 4 | **+ 50 µL compound at 4× final** — *round 2, the ligand* | **test** | 15 | 200 µL |

Volume goes 100 → 150 → 200 µL; compounds are added at 4× so they end at 1× in 200 µL.
VUAA1: 200 µM in the added 50 µL → **50 µM final**.

### Odorant concentrations are not known — the most serious limitation of this experiment

The odorants were supplied as aqueous solutions by another laboratory, whose stated practice was to
dilute those solutions **10,000-fold** for *Drosophila* odorant testing. That same 10,000-fold
dilution was applied here. **The concentration of the supplied solutions was not recorded, so the
molar concentration of every odorant in the well is unknown and cannot be reconstructed.**

Two consequences, both of which limit what any part page in this collection may claim:

1. **No odorant result can be placed on a dose axis.** Nothing in this collection may be described
   as under- or over-dosed, and no value may be compared against a published EC₅₀. Where an earlier
   draft of this documentation explained a null result by saying the dose was below the EC₅₀, that
   explanation was unfounded and has been removed.
2. **A dilution factor does not transfer between a fly assay and a cell assay.** In *Drosophila*
   work an odorant is diluted in oil or water and the animal is exposed to the **headspace above the
   liquid** — the stimulus is the vapour, which is orders of magnitude more dilute than the liquid
   it evaporated from. Here the cells sit **in the liquid** and meet the liquid concentration
   directly. The same "1:10,000" therefore denotes two different stimuli, and the convention was
   carried across formats without that being noticed.

**What a repeat requires before anything else:** the supplied stock's concentration in g/L or mol/L,
or odorants weighed out and dissolved to a known molarity, so that each receptor can be dosed in µM
around its own published EC₅₀.

Every well therefore carries **its own vehicle control in the same well** — round 1 is an identical
50 µL addition and plate transfer with no ligand. That is the strength of the design and also its
weakness: because the reported value is round 2 minus round 1, **anything that happens to the well
during round 1 is subtracted out of round 2 with the opposite sign.** A well that loses baseline
fluorescence in round 1 produces a large positive ΔF_corr with no ligand effect whatsoever. This
caught three wells on this plate; see the *Characterisation* entry.

**Pipetting:** an 8-channel pipette against a 12-column plate means two passes — columns 1–8, then
9–12, in the same fixed order every time. The resulting time offset is identical in both rounds and
cancels in the correction.

### Calculation

| quantity | definition |
|---|---|
| **F0** | mean of the 5 baseline cycles of that round |
| **F_MAX** | maximum of the 3-cycle moving average — a single-point maximum is positively biased |
| **ΔF_blank** | ( F_MAX(round 1) − F0a ) / F0a |
| **ΔF_test** | ( F_MAX(round 2) − F0b ) / F0b |
| **ΔF_corr** | ΔF_test − ΔF_blank |
| **ΔF_norm** | ΔF_corr ÷ ΔF_corr(VUAA1, same column) — reported but unusable, see *Discussion* |

Every part page reports **all three** of ΔF_blank, ΔF_test and ΔF_corr, never ΔF_corr alone.

### Gain QC — why two compounds are missing from every table

Detector gain on this instrument is **not stored in the protocol**; it is set in the Start
Measurement dialog and is lost whenever the protocol is edited. It was not held constant across all
32 reads of this session.

ΔF is a ratio **within one well**, so a different gain in a different row is harmless. But the `F0`
read and the response read it is divided by **must share a gain**. To test that without assuming it,
the untransfected wells (column 12), which should not respond to anything, were used as an absolute
yardstick:

| row | compound | median col-12 F0a | round 1 / F0a | round 2 / F0b | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | VUAA1 | 1610 | 0.998 | 0.951 | valid |
| **B** | **ethyl propionate** | 1408 | **1.348** | **1.366** | **discarded** — both pairs mismatched |
| **C** | **isopentyl acetate** | 551 | **3.117** | 1.017 | **discarded** — round 1 pair mismatched |
| D | 3-octanol | 2182 | 0.999 | 1.034 | valid |
| E | benzaldehyde | 1946 | 1.002 | 1.049 | valid |
| F | 2-heptanone | 2437 | 1.012 | 1.055 | valid |
| G | valeric acid | 1731 | 1.011 | 1.074 | valid |
| H | Control (buffer) | 18726 | 0.950 | 0.951 | valid (internally consistent; absolute gain ~10× the others, which does not affect a within-well ratio) |

**Two of eight compounds — ethyl propionate and isopentyl acetate — produced no usable data at all.**
This was the largest single loss in the experiment.

**Fix for anyone repeating this:** run gain adjustment once, **write the number down**, then type
that value manually into every subsequent read and leave `Gain Adjustment` unchecked for the rest of
the session.

### References

1. Zboray K, Mohamed Mahmoud M, Pató A, *et al.* Stable cell lines expressing *Drosophila* odorant receptors for the detection of plant pathogen-related volatile organic compounds. *Sci Rep* **13**, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4
2. BMG LABTECH SMART Control Software Manual Part II (0430F0049A, 2022-09-09) — §3.4 Data Output, §6.5 Plate Identification, §6.6 Sample IDs.

data.title: Four measured acceptance criteria, and the buffer-only well that satisfies three
data.value:
Before any per-part number can be read, two things had to be established: that the read-out works,
and how large a signal this plate produces **with nothing added**.

### 1. The read-out works

`BBa_26E11Z80` with no tuning receptor responded to 50 µM VUAA1 (ΔF\_corr +0.2148, ligand round
+0.1186, gradual) while untransfected cells in the same row gave +0.0041. The full data, kinetics,
controls and caveats are intrinsic to that part and are documented on `BBa_26E11Z80`.

### 2. Four acceptance criteria, all measured — none assumed

The untransfected wells (column 12: same additions, same handling, no receptor, every valid row)
give the noise of each quantity directly. Taking 3 SD of each:

| # | criterion                         | bound         | measured from                                                                                                                                                                                                         |               |                                                                     |
| - | --------------------------------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1 | ΔF\_corr ≥ **0.134**              | 3 × SD 0.0448 | untransfected ΔF\_corr, n \= 6                                                                                                                                                                                        |               |                                                                     |
| 2 | ΔF\_test ≥ **0.089**              | 3 × SD 0.0296 | untransfected ΔF\_test, n \= 6 — *the ligand round must itself rise*                                                                                                                                                  |               |                                                                     |
| 3 |                                   | ΔF\_blank     | ≤ **0.060**                                                                                                                                                                                                           | 3 × SD 0.0200 | untransfected ΔF\_blank, n \= 6 — *the vehicle round must be quiet* |
| 4 | frac\_at\_first\_read \< **0.60** | —             | shape: the fraction of the total rise already present at the first post-addition cycle. Near 1.0 means the change was complete before the plate finished re-inserting — an optical or physical step, not Ca²⁺ influx. |               |                                                                     |

**Criterion 3 is the one that is easy to forget and it changed several readings on this plate.**
Because ΔF\_corr \= round 2 − round 1, a well that *loses* baseline in round 1 reports a large
positive ΔF\_corr with no ligand effect at all. Three wells did exactly that.

### 3. Every condition over 0.134, decomposed

| compound                  | cell line | ΔF\_blank  | ΔF\_test   | ΔF\_corr   | frac | criteria failed                                  |
| ------------------------- | --------- | ---------- | ---------- | ---------- | ---- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| **Control (buffer only)** | **Or35a** | −0.096     | **+0.353** | **+0.449** | 0.16 | 3 only                                           |
| Control (buffer only)     | Or42a     | **−0.301** | +0.014     | +0.315     | —    | 2 and 3 — 95 % of the value is the vehicle round |
| valeric acid              | Or35a     | −0.117     | +0.177     | +0.295     | 0.87 | 3 and 4                                          |
| **valeric acid**          | **Or85b** | −0.013     | +0.204     | +0.217     | 0.59 | **none**                                         |
| VUAA1 50 µM               | ORCO only | −0.096     | +0.119     | +0.215     | 0.06 | 3 only                                           |
| 2-heptanone               | ORCO only | +0.025     | +0.210     | +0.186     | 0.83 | 4                                                |
| 2-heptanone               | Or7a      | **−0.164** | +0.020     | +0.184     | —    | 2 and 3 — 89 % of the value is the vehicle round |
| valeric acid              | ORCO only | +0.040     | +0.197     | +0.158     | 0.77 | 4                                                |
| benzaldehyde              | ORCO only | +0.027     | +0.165     | +0.138     | 0.90 | 4                                                |
| **VUAA1 50 µM**           | **Or35a** | +0.040     | +0.178     | +0.137     | 0.49 | **none**                                         |

### 4. The result that sets the ceiling on everything else

Row H received **plain assay buffer in both rounds**. Every well in it should read zero. The Or35a
well instead rose **+0.353 in round 2**, gradually, peaking at 96 s, giving ΔF\_corr **+0.449** — the
largest value on the plate, from a well that never saw a ligand. It satisfies criteria 1, 2 and 4
and fails only 3, and it fails 3 only narrowly (−0.096 against a −0.060 bound).

![Two line charts of fluorescence change over time for all 12 columns of the buffer-only row. In round 2, with only assay buffer added, the Or35a trace rises above the 0.134 threshold to +0.35; in round 1 the Or42a trace sits 30 % below its own baseline. The other ten columns stay within ±0.1.](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/9dfa1d46-443b-491e-b31d-f454c65f55ec/7fd45191845ab3fe49775a76fe355123055b9f553f63860d4e9f01b4aa63e0f9.avif "Buffer-only row, both rounds — the plate’s false positives")

*Row H, all 12 columns, both rounds, raw fluorescence as (F − F₀)/F₀ against time. Left: round 1.
Right: round 2 — also plain buffer. Or35a (blue) rises past the threshold in round 2 with no ligand
present. Or42a (orange) does the opposite: it loses 30 % of its baseline at the round-1 addition and
never recovers, which the subtraction then converts into a spurious +0.315. The ten grey traces are
the other columns, all within ±0.1.*

**This is the most important single result on the plate.** A buffer-only well produced a larger,
better-shaped signal than any odorant did. At n \= 1, the four criteria are **necessary but not
sufficient**, and no odorant response on this plate is distinguishable from the plate's own noise,
however good it looks. Two conditions pass all four criteria — valeric acid × Or85b (+0.217) and
VUAA1 × Or35a (+0.137) — and both are smaller than +0.449. They are documented on their part pages
as **conditions to repeat, not as hits**.

### 5. Full plate-level dataset, ΔF\_corr

Rows \= compound, columns \= tuning receptor co-transfected with `BBa_26E11Z80`.
**Bold** \= above 0.134. Blank rows: discarded by the gain QC. Each part page carries its own column
decomposed into ΔF\_blank / ΔF\_test / ΔF\_corr with its signal curves.

| compound             | Or7a       | Or19a  | Or22a  | Or35a      | Or42a      | Or59b  | Or67a  | Or67b  | Or85b      | Or98a  | ORCO only  | untransf. |
| -------------------- | ---------- | ------ | ------ | ---------- | ---------- | ------ | ------ | ------ | ---------- | ------ | ---------- | --------- |
| VUAA1 50 µM          | −0.055     | +0.023 | +0.049 | **+0.137** | −0.026     | −0.037 | −0.001 | +0.000 | +0.024     | −0.020 | **+0.215** | +0.004    |
| ethyl propionate     | —          | —      | —      | —          | —          | —      | —      | —      | —          | —      | —          | —         |
| isopentyl acetate    | —          | —      | —      | —          | —          | —      | —      | —      | —          | —      | —          | —         |
| 3-octanol            | +0.096     | +0.010 | −0.009 | +0.013     | −0.005     | +0.026 | +0.029 | +0.019 | +0.021     | +0.010 | +0.073     | +0.028    |
| benzaldehyde         | +0.120     | +0.027 | +0.036 | +0.045     | +0.068     | +0.048 | −0.014 | +0.040 | +0.023     | +0.037 | **+0.138** | +0.074    |
| 2-heptanone          | **+0.184** | +0.036 | +0.032 | +0.065     | +0.057     | +0.036 | +0.033 | +0.038 | −0.006     | +0.017 | **+0.186** | +0.042    |
| valeric acid         | −0.028     | +0.012 | −0.017 | **+0.295** | −0.006     | +0.003 | +0.010 | +0.000 | **+0.217** | +0.002 | **+0.158** | −0.010    |
| **Control (buffer)** | −0.031     | +0.056 | +0.127 | **+0.449** | **+0.315** | +0.065 | −0.134 | −0.085 | +0.060     | −0.016 | −0.017     | −0.055    |

data.title: What this plate establishes, what it does not, and the seven changes the next run needs
data.value:
### Established

**One thing.** The reporter fusion `BBa_26E11Z80` is expressed, reaches the plasma membrane, and
gates Ca²⁺ in response to an Orco agonist, in transiently transfected HEK293. That makes the
platform real. The caveats on the magnitude are on that part's page.

### Not established

**No odorant response was demonstrated for any of the ten tuning receptors.** Not "the receptors do
not work" — the experiment could not have detected it if they did. Four reasons, each sufficient
alone:

**1. Expression, not ligand choice, is the limiting factor.** VUAA1 acts on **Orco** and bypasses
the tuning receptor, so all eleven Orco-containing columns should have responded. Only two did:
ORCO-only (+0.215) and Or35a (+0.137). **Nine of eleven Orco-containing wells failed their own
positive control.** Whatever the tuning receptors would have done to an odorant, this plate was not
in a state to see it. Zboray *et al.* (2023) reported the same pattern in several of their lines and attributed it to
translation and ER-export bottlenecks.

**2. The delivered dose is unknown, so no null result can be interpreted.** The odorants came as
stock solutions of unrecorded concentration, diluted 10,000-fold by a convention borrowed from
*Drosophila* experiments in which the animal samples the vapour rather than the liquid (see the
*Experiment* entry). Against that, Zboray *et al.* (2023) report EC₅₀ = 68.9 µM for 2-heptanone on Or85b and reach a
VUAA1-normalised 0.55 only at 100 µM, and Or98a's reference ligand (6-methyl-5-hepten-2-one,
EC₅₀ 2.06 µM) was not on the plate at all. Whether this experiment landed above, below or near those
values cannot be determined from the records.

**3. The vehicle round is not inert, and the correction amplifies that.** Three wells moved more
than ±0.060 during round 1; in two of them the vehicle round supplied 89 % and 95 % of the reported
ΔF_corr. Mechanically this looks like cell loss or a bubble at the moment of addition — consistent
with an uncoated plate and a 2.5 h session — not like receptor behaviour.

**4. The odorant working solutions appear to differ physically from the assay buffer.** The
ORCO-only column has no tuning receptor and no odorant specificity. It nevertheless moved in **every**
odorant row and not in the buffer row, and all three of those movements are step-shaped
(frac 0.77–0.90):

| row | ORCO-only ΔF_test | frac |
|---|---|---|
| VUAA1 | +0.119 | 0.06 |
| 3-octanol | +0.121 | — |
| benzaldehyde | +0.165 | 0.90 |
| 2-heptanone | +0.210 | 0.83 |
| valeric acid | +0.197 | 0.77 |
| **Control (buffer)** | **−0.004** | — |

"Steps for every odorant solution, flat for plain buffer" is the signature of a property of the
solutions — refractive index, temperature, residual solvent, pH — not of receptor activation.
GCaMP6f's chromophore has a pKa near 7.1–7.2, so a small pH difference in a working solution is by
itself enough to shift fluorescence.

Add the buffer-only well that reached +0.449 (see *Characterisation*), and the honest summary is:
**this plate validated the read-out and measured its own noise floor. It did not test odorant
specificity.**

### A note on ΔF_norm

ΔF_norm (ΔF_corr ÷ the same column's VUAA1 value) is in the dataset but is **not usable for this
plate**: nine of eleven VUAA1 denominators are at or below the noise floor, so the quotient is a
ratio of two noise values. It becomes meaningful only once every column passes its VUAA1 control.

### The seven changes the next run needs, in order

1. **Fix the gain manually.** Adjust once, record the value, type it in for every read, leave
   `Gain Adjustment` unchecked. This cost two of eight compounds.
2. **Poly-D-lysine–coated plates.** Cells detached progressively on the uncoated plate over a 2.5 h
   session. This is the most likely source of both the 0.045 noise floor and the three round-1
   baseline collapses.
3. **Add a mock-odorant control row** — the identical dilution series and handling with no odorant
   in it. This directly tests reason 4. If the ORCO-only column steps in that row too, the
   odorant-row signals are solution artefacts and the question is settled.
4. **Establish the dose before anything else.** Get the stock concentration in g/L or mol/L from the
   supplier, or weigh the odorants out. Then dose Or85b with 2-heptanone and Or98a with
   6-methyl-5-hepten-2-one as dose series bracketing their EC₅₀, **in µM**. Until the dose is a
   number, every odorant result in this collection is uninterpretable, whichever way it came out.
5. **Keep total time in assay buffer under ~40 minutes**, even if that means four rows per plate
   instead of eight. This session ran 2.5 h.
6. **Raise expression, then re-test.** Zboray *et al.* (2023) induced with **1 µg/mL doxycycline, 48–72 h** before
   measurement and used selected stable clones; ours was a transient mixed population. Their
   responses were **1.24–4.62**, i.e. 6–21× ours.
7. **Blot before measuring again.** Every construct carries a detection handle — `BBa_262WP16P`,
   with His₆ and Xpress epitopes — and no blot has been run. An anti-His or anti-Xpress blot answers
   "was the protein made?" directly and splits the nine failing columns into a translation problem
   and a trafficking problem. It is the most informative next experiment and needs no plate reader.

### Replication status

**n = 1 for everything in this collection.** One well per condition, one plate, one day
(2026-10-10). No value here should be used as a reference figure.

### References

1. Zboray K, Mohamed Mahmoud M, Pató A, *et al.* Stable cell lines expressing *Drosophila* odorant receptors for the detection of plant pathogen-related volatile organic compounds. *Sci Rep* **13**, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4
2. Chen T-W, Wardill TJ, Sun Y, *et al.* Ultrasensitive fluorescent proteins for imaging neuronal activity. *Nature* **499**, 295–300 (2013).

metadata.name: BBa_26LLF3LM
metadata.title: Or35a-IRES-mCherry
metadata.description:
Bicistronic sensing module: Drosophila melanogaster odorant receptor Or35a (409 aa), an EMCV internal ribosome entry site, and mCherry, with a GCCACC Kozak. Needs promoter and polyA from the host vector.



One transcript gives two separate proteins: Or35a is translated cap-dependently, mCherry from the IRES as an independent expression marker. Downstream expression is expected to be lower than the upstream cistron - acceptable for a bright constitutive marker.



Or35a is expected to assemble with Orco into a heteromeric ligand-gated ion channel; odorant binding opens the channel and admits extracellular Ca2+. This part does not report the signal itself - a co-expressed Orco module with a calcium indicator is required.



Red fluorescence confirms the transcript is present, not receptor folding or trafficking; no epitope tag is included.

data.title: Why Or35a, and what is already known about it
data.value:
This module supplies one thing to the platform: **the ligand specificity of Or35a**. The pore, the
trafficking and the read-out all come from `BBa_26E11Z80`; the collection's *Design* entry covers
that split and the collection-wide choices (codon optimisation, the IRES-mCherry arrangement, the
Kozak, the absence of a promoter).

### Prior art for this receptor

No characterisation of Or35a in a mammalian heterologous system is known to us; it was not among
the 12 receptors examined by Zboray *et al.* (2023). **[TO FILL: strongest predicted ligands from DoOR 2.0]**

### What the odorant panel offered this receptor

**None of the six compounds tested has a published response for this receptor.** Zboray *et al.* (2023) either
did not test it or obtained no response, and the compounds that did respond in that study did so on
receptors that are not in this collection. Whether DoOR 2.0 predicts a response to any of the six is
**[TO FILL: check DoOR 2.0 for 3-octanol, benzaldehyde, 2-heptanone, valeric acid, isopentyl
acetate, ethyl propionate]**. The panel was, for this receptor, a blind screen.

The panel as a whole, and why it is weaker than it should be, is in the collection's *Design* entry.

### Source

The receptor coding sequence is `BBa_26HJ1RUT` — FlyBase accession, protein length and synthesis route are on
that part's page. The module adds an EMCV IRES and mCherry (Shaner *et al.* 2004) around it; the
whole construct was synthesised by GenScript in an IP-free pcDNA3.1(+) backbone.

### Use

Co-transfect with **`BBa_26E11Z80`**. Neither part is a sensor alone. For Or35a in your own expression
context, use the bare CDS `BBa_26HJ1RUT` instead.

mCherry from the IRES is the diagnostic that matters for this part specifically: red cells with no
calcium response localise the fault **downstream of transcription** — translation, folding or
trafficking — which is exactly the failure mode seen on this plate.

### Reference

Zboray K, Mohamed Mahmoud M, Pató A, *et al.* Stable cell lines expressing *Drosophila* odorant receptors for the detection of plant pathogen-related volatile organic compounds. *Sci Rep* **13**, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4

data.title: Or35a module: both measurement rounds for all six testable compounds
data.value:
Transiently co-transfected into HEK293 with `BBa_26E11Z80`, **one well per condition**, 2026-10-10. Thresholds: ΔF\_corr ≥ 0.134, ΔF\_test ≥ 0.089, |ΔF\_blank| ≤ 0.060, frac < 0.60 — all four
measured on this plate's untransfected wells and defined in the collection documentation (*Drosophila odorant receptor calcium-reporter platform*), together with the full conditions.

| compound                             | final conc. | ΔF\_blank | ΔF\_test | **ΔF\_corr**  | reading                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------- | --------- | -------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| VUAA1                                | 50 µM       | +0.0403   | +0.1776  | **+0.1373**   | **passes all four criteria**, but frac 0.49 sits just inside the 0.60 bound — only marginally gradual (peak 84 s)                                           |
| 3-octanol                            | 1:10,000    | +0.0193   | +0.0324  | **+0.0130**   | below the 0.134 threshold — no response detected                                                                                                            |
| benzaldehyde                         | 1:10,000    | -0.0098   | +0.0355  | **+0.0453**   | below the 0.134 threshold — no response detected                                                                                                            |
| 2-heptanone                          | 1:10,000    | -0.0402   | +0.0246  | **+0.0648**   | below the 0.134 threshold — no response detected                                                                                                            |
| valeric acid                         | 1:10,000    | -0.1172   | +0.1774  | **+0.2946**   | over 0.134 but **fails criterion 3/4**: the vehicle round moved -0.117, outside the ±0.060 bound (40% of ΔF\_corr is that movement); step-shaped, frac 0.87 |
| Control (buffer only)                | —           | -0.0961   | +0.3525  | **+0.4486**   | over 0.134 but **fails criterion 3**: the vehicle round moved -0.096, outside the ±0.060 bound (21% of ΔF\_corr is that movement)                           |
| ethyl propionate · isopentyl acetate | 1:10,000    | —         | —        | not evaluable | gain changed between the baseline and response reads in those two rows; both discarded by the QC in the collection's *Experiment* entry                     |

*Both measurement rounds for this well, raw fluorescence expressed as (F − F₀)/F₀ against time after the 50 µL addition. **Left:** round 1, plain assay buffer — the vehicle control for every trace on the right. **Right:** round 2, the compound. The quoted ΔF\_corr is the right-hand peak minus the left-hand peak, so a trace that sags on the left inflates it.*

**Positive control for this column.** VUAA1 at 50 µM acts on Orco and does not require Or35a, so it
tests whether this well was expressing at all. It **passed cleanly**: ΔF\_corr +0.1373, ligand round +0.1776, vehicle round +0.0403, frac 0.49.

Plate-level context — the buffer-only control row, the decomposition of every above-threshold
condition, and the full 6 × 12 matrix — is in the collection's *Characterisation* entry.![Two line charts for the Or35a well. In round 2 the buffer-only trace rises highest of all, to +0.35 with no ligand present, above the valeric-acid trace at +0.18.](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/c09e424a-254d-42f7-9b0b-b8ba0e48659e/e1744bf44e6cd89061da7727bb78cc95da8b89139a0cf917580be4ce92a7012f.avif "Or35a — both measurement rounds, six compounds")

data.title: What the experiment does and does not establish for Or35a
data.value:
**This column is simultaneously the collection's one clean VUAA1 response in a tuning-receptor
well and its worst false positive. Both readings come from the same two wells and must be reported
together.**

**The good result.** VUAA1 gave ΔF_corr +0.1373 with ΔF_test +0.1776, ΔF_blank +0.0403 and frac 0.49
— it passes all four acceptance criteria, though frac 0.49 is close to the 0.60 bound and the rise
is only marginally gradual. Only two of the eleven Orco-containing columns responded
to the positive control at all, and this is one of them, so the construct was expressed here. That
makes this column the best candidate in the collection for a clean repeat.

**The result that cancels any odorant claim.** The buffer-only well in this same column — nothing
but assay buffer in both rounds — rose **+0.3525 in round 2**, gradually, peaking at 96 s, giving
ΔF_corr **+0.4486**. That is the largest value on the entire plate, and it is larger than this
column's valeric-acid well (ΔF_corr +0.2946, of which 40 % is a −0.117 round-1 collapse and whose
rise is step-shaped at frac 0.87).

So in this one column, a well with no ligand out-performed the well with ligand, on both magnitude
and shape. **No odorant conclusion can be drawn here at n = 1**, and the valeric-acid value should
not be quoted as a response.

What this column justifies is a repeat: coated plate, replicates, a mock-odorant row, and VUAA1 as
the per-column normaliser it was meant to be.

### Replication status

**n = 1.** One well per condition, one plate, one day. Two further compounds (ethyl propionate,
isopentyl acetate) were lost to the gain fault documented in the collection's *Experiment* entry.
Nothing here constrains the receptor itself — only this construct, in this chassis, at these
concentrations, on this plate.

### Reference

Zboray K, Mohamed Mahmoud M, Pató A, *et al.* Stable cell lines expressing *Drosophila* odorant receptors for the detection of plant pathogen-related volatile organic compounds. *Sci Rep* **13**, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4

data.title: A bare Or85b CDS: what it is for and what it needs
data.value:
**This is a building block, not a device.** Or85b binds odorant but has no pore and cannot reach the
plasma membrane on its own: it requires the co-receptor Orco, which supplies both (`BBa_26LWIKBQ`,
or the reporter fusion `BBa_26E11Z80`). Expressed alone it stays in the ER.

### When to use this part rather than the module

Use **this CDS** when assembling Or85b into your own expression context — your own promoter, tag,
fluorescent marker or polycistronic design. Use **`BBa_26K1TU11`** instead for a ready bicistronic unit with a
GCCACC Kozak and an IRES-mCherry expression marker already in place.

As supplied, this part needs a promoter, a Kozak (or an upstream in-frame fusion) and a polyA.

### Why codon-optimised

The reasoning is collection-wide and is documented in the collection documentation (*Drosophila odorant receptor calcium-reporter platform*): Zboray *et al.* (2023) used wild-type OR sequences, found
translation to be a likely bottleneck in HEK293, and recommended codon optimisation. Every receptor
CDS in this collection follows that recommendation.

### Source

| | |
|---|---|
| Organism | *Drosophila melanogaster* |
| Reference gene | FlyBase **FBgn0037590** |
| Reference transcript | FlyBase **FBtr0081900** |
| RefSeq protein | **NP_524279** |
| Encoded protein | **390 aa, identical to the FlyBase reference** — only the codons differ |
| How obtained | codon-optimised for human expression and **synthesised by GenScript**, delivered in an IP-free version of the pcDNA3.1(+) backbone |

Not cloned from flies, and not evolved or computationally designed: this is the native
*D. melanogaster* protein sequence, back-translated with human codon usage.

### Characterisation status

**Not characterised in isolation**, and it cannot meaningfully be — a tuning receptor alone produces
no signal, so there is no signal curve to show on this page. Functional testing was done on `BBa_26K1TU11`
co-transfected with `BBa_26E11Z80`; the signal curves, the three ΔF values per compound, the
acceptance criteria and the controls are on that part's page, and what is known about Or85b from the
literature is recorded there too. Repeating any of it here would duplicate content across parts,
which the Registry's documentation guidance asks authors not to do.

### Reference

Zboray K, Mohamed Mahmoud M, Pató A, *et al.* Stable cell lines expressing *Drosophila* odorant receptors for the detection of plant pathogen-related volatile organic compounds. *Sci Rep* **13**, 21757 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-47455-4
